units.title: DNA, RNA and protein synthesis
units.why: Molecular biology explains how genetic information is stored and expressed.
examples: A pairs with T and C with G in DNA
misconceptions: DNA directly becomes a protein without RNA
solutions: RNA has ribose/uracil and is usually single-stranded

videoPackage.title: From DNA to protein
videoPackage.transcript: We follow information from DNA through transcription to translation and connect codons to amino-acid sequences.

units.title: Human and plant reproduction
units.why: Reproduction maintains populations and connects cell division to development.
examples: pollen carries male gamete to stigma
zygote divides by mitosis during development
misconceptions: pollination is the same as fertilisation
solutions: transfer of pollen; fertilisation is fusion

videoPackage.title: Reproduction and development
videoPackage.transcript: We compare plant and human reproduction, keep pollination distinct from fertilisation, and track chromosome number through development.

units.title: Natural selection and evidence
units.why: Evolution explains biological diversity through inherited variation and changing environments.
principles: heritable variation affects survival and reproduction
individuals do not evolve because they need to
examples: antibiotic resistance increases when resistant bacteria survive treatment

videoPackage.title: Selection across generations
videoPackage.transcript: We distinguish individual survival from population change and use antibiotic resistance as an evidence-based example of selection.

units.title: Classification and biodiversity
units.why: Classification organises life and makes biodiversity patterns understandable.
principles: classification reflects shared characteristics and ancestry
a species can interbreed to produce fertile offspring
biodiversity includes genetic, species and ecosystem variety
examples: binomial names use genus and species

videoPackage.title: Organising biodiversity
videoPackage.transcript: We move from species to kingdoms, interpret a simple tree of relatedness, and connect classification to conservation.

units.title: Population and community ecology
units.why: Population ecology helps explain limits, competition and sustainable management.
examples: predator-prey numbers fluctuate with a lag
misconceptions: carrying capacity is a fixed universal number

videoPackage.title: Populations in balance
videoPackage.transcript: We read population curves, identify limiting factors, and connect interactions to sustainable decisions.
